as_told.title: 1971 agreement: red phone invented to stop UFOs triggering nuclear war

plain: The United States and the Soviet Union are said to have signed an agreement, still in force, in which each side promised to tell the other if UFOs interfered with its missile early warning systems, the radars that watch for a nuclear attack. A guest named Karl Nell, speaking as an official, describes it as a pact meant "to reduce the threat of nuclear war" with a clause that "either side will notify the other if UFOs impact their missile early warning systems." A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown dates it to about 1971 and calls it an outer space treaty in which the two nations agree to notify each other when they detect UFOs. A former CIA contractor, Bob Maguire, puts it in 1971 under President Richard Nixon, during the arms talks between the two powers, and goes further: he says the "red phone," the emergency hotline between the two capitals, "was invented to stop UFOs from starting thermonuclear war." The point, as they tell it, is that both superpowers took UFOs seriously enough to write them into nuclear safety rules.
